environmental_concerns: Virgin grade (Grade 1) relies on wood pulp; coatings/waxing can reduce recyclability
Coated or laminated variants harder to recycle
Coatings for barrier properties may reduce compostability

recycled_content_possible: Yes (min 60% non-bamboo/hardwood/softwood pulp OR 100% waste paper for ECO Mark)
environmental_advantages: ECO Mark variant must be recyclable/reusable/biodegradable

plastic_content: No (paper-foil, but often laminated with plastic/adhesive)
waste_management_route: Limited - typically non-recyclable in standard MRF streams
environmental_advantages: Excellent barrier properties reduce food waste
environmental_concerns: Multi-material laminate structure impedes recycling; separating aluminium from paper/adhesive is difficult
Wax/plastic coatings for moisture resistance reduce recyclability

recycled_content_possible: Not applicable (natural fibre, not from recycled content)
environmental_advantages: Renewable, biodegradable, reusable, traditional low-impact material
environmental_concerns: Lower moisture barrier than plastic; may require moisture-proof liner for some grains

material_name: Rigid plastic packaging (Category I, e.g. PET/HDPE bottles, jars)
waste_management_route: Rigid plastic recycling stream (EPR Category I)
environmental_concerns: Petroleum-derived; requires EPR compliance and collection infrastructure

material_name: Flexible plastic packaging - single/multilayer (Category II, e.g. PE/PP pouches, carry bags)
recycled_content_possible: Limited (single-layer flexible more recyclable than multilayer)
end_of_life_option: EPR-mandated collection; energy recovery for non-recyclable fraction
waste_management_route: Flexible plastic recycling stream (EPR Category II) where infrastructure exists
environmental_advantages: Lightweight, low material use per package
environmental_concerns: Multilayer flexible plastics with different resin types are difficult to recycle

material_name: Multilayered plastic packaging (Category III, e.g. metallised/laminate pouches)
plastic_content: Yes (partial, at least one plastic layer)
end_of_life_option: Non-recyclable fraction phased out within 2 years per rules; else energy recovery
environmental_advantages: Excellent barrier properties (extends shelf life, reduces food waste)
environmental_concerns: Non-recyclable MLP being phased out under Plastic Waste Management Rules

renewable_resource: Often (bio-based feedstocks, e.g. PLA, starch blends)
environmental_advantages: Biodegradable under controlled composting conditions, reduces persistent plastic waste
environmental_concerns: Requires industrial composting facilities; may not degrade in home composting or natural environments
